description: I am a solo participant interested in AI, data science/analysis, health research, and space exploration. My experience includes working with public-health data, creating visualizations, working with big data and building AI tools that answer questions using cited sources.
summary: Fire behaves differently in reduced gravity, and results from one experiment can be hard to apply to another. OMNION is a dashboard for exploring NASA combustion research. Ask a question about flame spread, ignition, detection, or extinction, and a browser-based AI model ranks relevant passages from seven studies. Each result shows what was measured, the test conditions, and a link to the original source. A worked Saffire-II example compares two published runs and lets users check the chart, table, and downloadable data. OMNION helps students and researchers see which findings apply to their question and where the available evidence runs out.
details:
OMNION helps students and researchers find evidence about spacecraft fire behavior. Enter a question, filter by topic or gravity regime, and open a study to see its findings, experimental conditions, limits, and original source. MiniLM runs in the browser and ranks reviewed passages using semantic similarity and keyword matching. The dashboard also supports keyword search when the model cannot load.

In the Saffire-II example, NASA reported a flame spread rate of 2.1 mm/s at 20 cm/s airflow and 2.6 mm/s at 25 cm/s airflow. Both cotton–fiberglass runs used the same reported oxygen level, fabric geometry, flow direction, and ignition setting. The observed difference was 0.5 mm/s. Users can compare the runs in a chart or table, download the CSV, and check both values against Table 1 of NASA’s results presentation. Establishing a safe airflow setting would require separate evidence.

OMNION puts each observation next to the conditions that qualify it. For example, a question about Mars gravity shows an evidence gap in this collection. The prototype uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Transformers.js, and ONNX Runtime Web. The packaged build runs on a laptop without an API key.

AI disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, SVG interface graphics, source summaries, data transcription, and drafting the submission and slides. MiniLM ranks reviewed evidence at runtime. The two measured values were checked against NASA’s original table. The flight photograph comes from NASA’s SoFIE-GEL experiment imagery.
